proposals: NSE and BSE should publish a free, machine-readable security master that tags every listed instrument by type — equity, bond, REIT unit — with its ISIN, so that bonds trading near ₹1,00,000 face values cannot contaminate an equity analysis, the error this post had to correct.

NSE and BSE should publish, for every listed equity, the number of days it actually traded in each calendar year, so that the thin trading behind this post’s 26.6% coverage of the ₹0–50 band is visible as an exchange statistic rather than discovered as a data gap.

The exchanges should publish split, bonus and other corporate-action adjustment factors in a downloadable file for every listed equity, going back to listing, so that independent studies of price-band migration over windows like January 2023 to August 2026 can separate real price moves from mechanical ones.

SEBI should require the exchanges to publish complete daily price histories for stocks suspended or delisted during any period, so that studies like this one, which could track only 12 of 38 stocks above ₹10,000, are not limited to survivors with unbroken records.
